title: Reader -> Executor handoff (bundle.handoff/v2)
description: Formalizes the Reader->Executor contract (STEP 16). Documents the v2 shape that bundle.handoff.HandoffV2 (de)serializes; legacy file-watch handshakes (resultsDbURL.properties/insert.sql/args/fwVar.shift/runmefirstonce.first, see py_executor.read_handshake) are converted into this same model by bundle.handoff.handoff_from_legacy — neither Reader nor Executor behaviour changes in this step.

protocol.description: Schema identifier, "<name>/v<major>". Readers reject any value whose name or major differs.

language.description: Candidate runtime the Executor must launch.

candidate_transport.description: How candidate sources are delivered. "loose-files" is today's <combi_id>_0_0.* directory; "sharded" packs candidates into *.fwshard containers; "grpc" streams candidates live to the Executor's gRPC ingestion server (no on-disk candidate source).

id_format.description: Pattern describing how candidate IDs are encoded in filenames/paths, e.g. "<combi_id>_0_0".

sources.description: Locations the Executor reads candidates from (loose-files: a single directory; sharded: the shard directory; grpc: the endpoint the candidates were streamed to — informational, nothing to re-read locally).

result_schema_mode.description: Opaque descriptor of the results-row shape derived from the legacy insert.sql template, e.g. "placeholders=9". Never the SQL text itself.

verdict_mode.description: FW_VAR vs FW_CUSTOM_VAR, chosen by legacy convention from the '?' count of insert.sql (== 6 -> custom).

custom_verdicts.description: Explicit FW_CUSTOM_VAR code/message pairs; empty unless verdict_mode is FW_CUSTOM_VAR.

shift.description: FW_VAR positional shift (legacy: arguments/fwVar.shift). P6: never empty/absent; defaults to 1.

preprocess.description: Optional RunMeFirstOnce preprocessor reference (legacy: runFirstOnce/runmefirstonce.first). Java-only; ignored for Python candidates.

execution_policy_ref.description: Reference to the execution policy governing this run (sandbox backend, resource limits — STEP 27). Not the policy body itself.

result_target_ref.description: Connection coordinates for the results DB. NEVER carries a password — credentials are resolved at runtime from BundleConfig/environment (legacy: resultsDbURL.properties' jdbc URL, with its password stripped).
